name: paged
description:
The regression test for the alerts request having no paging at all. The endpoint used to be posted once with an empty {} body, so whatever a single unpaged response carried was the entire import and every alert past it was invisible.

Cyberint pages POST /alert/api/v1/alerts with a 1-based `page` and a `size`, both top-level fields of the request body, and answers with `total` -- the count across ALL pages -- alongside `alerts`. There is no cursor. The contract comes from four agreeing implementations, two of them Cyberint's own: github.com/CyberInt/servicenow-integration (fetchAlerts(page) posts {page, size, filters} and loops on the returned total), github.com/CyberInt/qradar-universal-cloud-rest-api (posts {"page": 1, "size": ...} literally), Check Point's Splunk SOAR app, and the Cortex XSOAR pack.

Three pages, matched on the page number in the POST body, so a walk that failed to advance starves on page 2 rather than quietly passing. Every route is when_exhausted:error, so no request may repeat. Each page carries a slice of a declared total of 7, and reaching that count is what ends the walk -- which is the terminator Cyberint's own ServiceNow client uses, since `total` counts matching alerts across every page rather than the length of one.

The assertions that matter are the domains that exist only on pages 2 and 3: page2-only.example.com and page3-only.example.com. A single-request import produces one asset and this scenario fails on all three counts. requests_absent proves no fourth page is requested once the count is satisfied.

namespaced_ids is skipped: the foreign id is the dash-substituted domain, which carries no tenant scope -- a domain name is globally meaningful, so two tenants importing one domain landing on one asset is arguably correct.
